register.headline: Couzo's new packing of 130 squares from PR #574's, 2.05e-3 below T-174
register.source_checks: The issue says both of the source's exact checkers accept the certificate in exact rational arithmetic: verify_bound_certificate.py, Evan Daniel's MIT separating-axis verifier with modifications by Francisco Couzo with Codex, byte-identical to the copy the issue-678 packet retains (valid and strictly valid, 1,624 candidate pairs), and exact_finish.py, an exact corner replay; both read the same certificate format. The source's commit of 27 October says the packing was read from a database salvaged after a host crash of 26 October and ends with a Co-Authored-By trailer naming Claude; the issue says Claude did the certification, the comparison and the report at the author's direction. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
register.credit: Credit Francisco Couzo (https://github.com/franciscouzo/square-packing), after the packing his searches started from, PR #574's at 130: found by Nate Chaoweeraprasit (itsnaka), improved by Siddharth Gupta and PingYou Ltd, as the issue asks. The issue says thirteen successive improvements of his live searches of 24 and 25 October took the side from 11.904483032516 to this one, ten by the web app's fq quench (a browser adaptation of Evan Daniel's fq optimizer), two by its basin hopping and one by native SLP, all on his own computers, and that matched one to one against PR #574's packing the largest move is 0.704, 11 squares move beyond 0.1 and 26 beyond 0.01, so it calls it a new packing found from #574's. A Kaggle per-puzzle side the issue quotes, 11.902430646006 for the team Cats and boxes, states no packing and is no report.
register.next_rung: Independently review the retained replay and the certificate (stage 4): a clean-room exact checker, the identity against the house's packing and the lineage the source states, a mapped review whose acceptance would raise both rungs.
